problem:
An inner product on $V={R}^{3}$ is given by $⟨x,y⟩=2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+9{x}_{3}{y}_{3}.$ Find $⟨x,y⟩$, if

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,y=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Inner Product of Two Vectors
examples.problem:
An inner product on $V = \mathbb{R}^3$ is given by $\langle \mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y} \rangle =  3 x_1 y_1 + x_2 y_2 + 7 x_3 y_3.$ Find $\langle \mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y} \rangle,$ if
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14054904/assets/028bb3befd54071fcae6cb88bd3e054d3325557ef31274ec23146e1da81f8258.png)
examples.worked_solution:
Computing the inner product according to the definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y⟩ & =3{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+7{x}_{3}{y}_{3} \\  & =3\cdot 1\cdot (-3)+(-2)\cdot 1+7\cdot 0\cdot 5 \\  & =-9-2+0 \\  & =-11.\end{aligned}
$$
